text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

The all-male panel is weak evidence on its own. In municipal planning leadership, all-male panels are statistically unremarkable and arise routinely without bias — so it tells you little, and leading with it makes you look like you're reaching.

Your stronger facts are the credential gap (master's plus licence plus twelve years, versus a bachelor's) and the two-week silence on a reasonable written request. Those stand independently and are harder to wave away.

So: press on process. Re-send the request, cite any policy or statutory timeline, ask what criteria were weighted and how. Note panel composition factually if you escalate, but as context, not as your argument.

What the answer reveals should set your next step.
